title: CRM Lite message envelope, v1
description: The single wire format for every CRM Lite command and event (ADR-017 §5). Deliberately broker-agnostic: no field here is Kafka-specific, and the same envelope would travel unchanged over another transport. Implemented by com.crm.messaging.contract.EventEnvelope.

messageId.description: Globally unique id of this message; doubles as the eventId. A redelivery carries the SAME value — it is what the receiving Inbox's UNIQUE (message_id, consumer_group) constraint keys on.

messageType.description: The contract name, e.g. crm.order.order-submitted. Never a Java class name: a class name is a refactoring hazard on the wire.

schemaVersion.description: Version of the payload contract. A consumer accepts a range and rejects anything outside it rather than guessing (ADR-017 §5.3).

aggregateType.description: The owning aggregate. Also the Debezium Outbox Event Router's routing field.

aggregateId.description: The aggregate's business identity — e.g. the KR-12 order number or the KR-11 account number. Never a database surrogate key.

sagaId.description: The sale-scoped orchestration id. For the SALE saga this IS the client's Idempotency-Key (ADR-016 §10), so the saga and the idempotency key are one value rather than two ids meaning the same thing.

correlationId.description: The end-to-end request id (X-Correlation-Id), already an MDC field in every service — so the log line about the HTTP request and the log line about the message it produced are the same search.

causationId.description: The messageId of the message that CAUSED this one. Null for a message originating from a synchronous request.

occurredAt.description: ISO-8601 UTC instant at which the business fact happened — NOT when it was published. The two differ by exactly the time the outbox row waited.

payload.description: The versioned contract body as JSON TEXT, not a nested object. Text because the consumer decodes it into a DTO the consumer owns (ADR-017 §6); a nested object would invite a shared payload type, which is the coupling this design refuses.
